Meccan, according to all.

One: it is split open.

The second: it falls. The poet said:

"They were the lofty sky of the people, but it split apart, and the gathering was left with no pillars raised for it."

The second: they are mixed together so that they become one sea. This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: they are seven seas, and they become one sea.(p-221)

The third: their sweet water is made to burst into their salt water, and their salt water into their sweet water, said by Qatadah.

It may also bear a fourth meaning: that is, they overflow.

﴿And when the graves are overturned﴾ has three meanings:

The first: they are searched and turned over, said by Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ikrimah. al-Farra' said: what is in their bellies of gold and silver is brought out, and this is one of the signs of the Hour, that the earth brings forth its gold and silver and then brings forth the dead.

The second: they are stirred for the Resurrection, said by al-Suddi.

The third: those who are in them of the dead are raised, said by Qatadah.

﴿A soul will know what it has sent forward and left behind﴾ has three meanings:

The first: what it did and what it neglected, said by Abu Razin.

The second: what it sent forward of obedience and left behind of the right of Allah, said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The third: what it sent forward of charities and left behind of inheritance.

It may also mean what it sent forward of disobedience and left behind of obedience, since it is brought forth in the manner of a warning. This is the answer to ﴿When the sky splits asunder﴾, since it is a statement. al-Hasan made it an oath, with ﴿A soul will know﴾ and what follows as its answer.

The more apparent view, held by the majority, is that it is a statement and not an oath.

﴿O man, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?﴾ Regarding "man" here there are three opinions: The first: it refers to every disbeliever.

The second: it refers to Ubayy ibn Khalaf, said by 'Ikrimah.

The third: it refers to Abu al-Ashadd ibn Kaladah ibn Asad al-Jumahi, said by Ibn 'Abbas.

Regarding what deceived him there are two sayings:

One: his enemy, Satan, said by Qatadah.

The second: his ignorance, which is the saying of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.(p-222)

It may also bear a third saying: that it is his being given respite.

﴿the Generous﴾: the One who overlooks and pardons. al-Hasan narrated that when 'Umar ibn al-Khattab recited ﴿O man﴾ ... the verse, he said: "his folly and his ignorance."

﴿Who created you, then proportioned you, then made you balanced﴾ may bear three meanings:

The first: He made your form proportionate and your creation balanced.

The second: He made your limbs proportionate according to need and balanced them in correspondence, so that one hand does not exceed the other, nor one foot the other.

The third: He proportioned you as a noble human being and turned you away from being made a beast of burden.

The people of insight (ashab al-khawatir) said: He proportioned you with reason and balanced you with faith.

﴿In whatever form He willed, He assembled you﴾ has three sayings: The first: He assembled you in whatever resemblance of mother, father, maternal uncle or paternal uncle, said by Mujahid.

The second: in beauty or ugliness, tallness or shortness, male or female, said by Ibn 'Isa.

The third: in whatever form of creation He assembled you, until you became in the form in which you are, O man, nothing among the animals resembling you.

He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what would be born to me? Either a boy or a girl." The Messenger of Allah said: "And whom would he resemble?" He said: "Either his father or his mother." Then he (peace be upon him) said to him: "Mah! Do not say such a thing. When the drop settles in the womb, Allah brings forth every lineage between it and Adam. Have you not read in the Book of Allah: ﴿In whatever form He willed, He assembled you﴾?" ﴿No! Rather, you deny the Recompense﴾ has three interpretations:(p-223)

The first: with the reckoning and the requital, said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: with justice and decree, said by 'Ikrimah.

The third: with the religion that Muhammad (ﷺ) brought, related by Ibn 'Isa.

﴿Noble recorders﴾ has three meanings:

The first: noble with Allah, said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The second: noble through faith, said by al-Suddi.

The third: because they do not leave the son of Adam except in two situations, at the place of relieving oneself and during intercourse, when they turn away from him. They record what he says, and therefore speaking during relieving oneself and intercourse is disliked.

It may also bear a fourth meaning: noble in discharging the trust regarding what they record of his deeds, so that they neither add to it nor subtract from it.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 82, verses 13–19:

Regarding His saying, ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss﴾ and ﴿indeed, the wicked will be in the Blazing Fire﴾, there are two opinions:

The first: it refers to the Hereafter, so the bliss of the righteous is in Paradise through reward, and the blazing fire of the wicked is in Hellfire through punishment.

The second opinion: that it refers to this world. On this view there are four aspects, mentioned by the scholars of the Khawatir (the people of spiritual insights).

The first: the bliss is contentment (qana'ah), and the blazing fire is greed (tama').

The second: the bliss is reliance upon God (tawakkul), and the blazing fire is covetousness (hirs).

The third: the bliss is being pleased with the decree (al-rida bi'l-qada'), and the blazing fire is discontent with what He has decreed and ordained.

The fourth: the bliss is in obedience, and the blazing fire is in disobedience.

Regarding His saying, ﴿And they will not be absent from it﴾, there are two aspects:

The first: "from the Day of Resurrection," as confirmation of the Resurrection. On this view, the address may be directed to both the righteous and the wicked together.

The second: "from the Fire," and the address is directed to the wicked alone, not the righteous. The meaning of their not being absent from it involves two matters:

The first: the confirmation of the threat.

The second: the eternal abiding of the wicked.

Regarding His saying, ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is? Then, what will make you know what the Day of Judgment is?﴾, it means the Day of Recompense, which is the Day of Resurrection. Regarding its repetition, there are two aspects:

The first: to magnify its matter and glorify its affair.

The second aspect: the first address is to the wicked and the second address is to the righteous, as encouragement.

Regarding His saying, ﴿The Day when no soul will have power for another soul at all﴾, it means that no created being has power to benefit or harm another created being.

Regarding His saying, ﴿And the command, that Day, belongs to God﴾, there are two aspects:

The first: concerning the recompense of reward and punishment.

The second: concerning the punishment and retribution.
